name: LEGALFLY agents
operator: LEGALFLY (the vendor); each customer is the operator of its own use
basis: LEGALFLY's own public pages (product, documentation, blog, customer stories, legal and security pages)
what: Platform of legal agents (Discovery, Review, Draft, Multi Review, Legal Radar, Translation) plus Agent Studio, where customers build multi-step workflows with triggers, conditions, approvals and notifications.
note: A scan of a product as its vendor documents it, not of any one deployment. Made by the report studio: a researcher-assessor, a challenger, then the scorer. From the studio's Web Summit 2026 agents list.
grant_note: Not measured. No deployment shape for this product is published in the capability grammar.

I07.n: Discovery retrieves and summarises connected data to answer questions; it does not change the records it reads.
I07.span: Discovery can retrieve and summarize Salesforce data

I08.n: Pre-built Agent Studio workflows are described as taking actions, such as redlining related documents and emailing the results.
I08.span: redlines related documents and emails you the results

I10.n: Discovery can search connected SharePoint and Google Drive folders alongside LEGALFLY's own sources.
I10.span: Connect SharePoint and Google Drive to access your documents directly in LEGALFLY.

I11.n: Discovery connects to a customer's Salesforce org through an MCP integration after per-user authorisation.
I11.span: Through the Discovery agent's Salesforce MCP integration

I16.n: In Review the agent proposes redrafts and a reviewer chooses to apply each one.
I16.span: When a reviewer applies a suggested redraft during a contract review

I17.n: A pre-built workflow answers routine mailbox questions and sends anything not covered to Legal for approval.
I17.span: with Legal approving anything not clearly covered

I20.n: Each agent's purpose is stated on the agents page, for example Discovery for research and advice.
I20.span: Legally trained agent for research and advice grounded in verified sources

I22.n: The help centre states a limit for users: Discovery's Salesforce integration reads records and cannot create, update or delete them; the security FAQ also says anonymisation can hide needed context and how to adjust it.

I36.n: The trust centre lists a request-only document titled for EU AI Act Article 50 transparency information, which identifies that provision; the document itself was not read.
I36.span: EU AI Act Article 50 - Technical Documentation and Transparency Information

I38.n: Workflow builders can place approval and review steps before a workflow continues.
I38.span: Set approval and review steps where a decision is needed

I57.n: The public help centre offers a way to submit a request to LEGALFLY support.

I58.n: The sources Legal Radar monitors are described by type of institution.
I58.span: We monitor the published updates from a jurisdiction's main institutions

I61.n: The trust centre lists subprocessors, including Anthropic and OpenAI as AI inference providers, with data locations.
I61.span: Processes pseudonymised content only, unless a customer explicitly enables
